content_html:
Reconciling External and Internal

The Relational/Co‑Arising View

“External” and “internal” look irreconcilable when treated as separate realms. The relational (or co‑arising) view shows how world and mind meet in an interface: perception and meaning emerge from interactions among body, environment, memory, attention, and culture.

Reconciling “external” and “internal” means shifting to the relational view: mind and world co‑specify each other through ongoing interaction. Photographs, like memories, gain meaning in this middle space.

Inputs flow from world → interface → mind; intentions and predictions flow back. The “external–internal split” is re‑framed as a bidirectional coupling where meaning emerges.

How Each Layer Contributes

Layer What It Provides Risk if Over‑Emphasised Photography Example
External Physical causes, constraints, shared references Naïve realism (“the image is the truth”) Forensics, journalism: indexing events
Relational Context, culture, language; action–perception loop Relativism if context is unconstrained Captioning, curation, social media frames
Internal Valence, memory, narrative identity Solipsism (“it’s only my feeling”) Personal albums, therapeutic imagery
